newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds rise in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds rise in dull trade.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Thursday in thin trading led by a rise in long-CPI-linked bonds, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.03 pct to 101.73
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.01 pct to 101.06.
Volume was low at 115 million shekels.
"The main reason for the ongoing rise of bonds is that mutual funds have money that they need to invest in bonds," said Danni Scharia at Capital Securities.
"The steady rise of long-inflation-linked bonds continued today. These bonds were the main gainers as there are not enough sellers in the market," said Miri Dagan at Clal Insurance.
Traders noted that investors focus on long-CPI-bonds because unlinked bonds have become less attractive following a recent decline in yields.
"Unlinked bonds were mixed with prices closing only slightly higher. The Makams closed almost unchanged with yields on the Makam for one year rising to 14.1 percent," Dagan added.
Dollar-linked bonds soared for the second day in a row. The U.S. currency continued to rise against the shekel climbing on Thursday above 3.3 shekels for the first time since June.
In the local foreign currency market the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3030 shekels against 3.2970 shekels on Wednesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
